name: Meter
description: Shows a measurement within a known range, such as disk usage, password strength or battery level. Use <meter> for a value that can go up or down; for progress toward finishing a task, use a Progress bar.
summary: Shows a measurement within a known range
researchNote: A value within a known range

elements.name: Label
elements.description: Names what is measured; linked with <label for>

elements.name: Track
elements.description: The full range from min to max

elements.name: Fill
elements.description: Its length shows the current value

elements.name: Value text
elements.description: The value in words or numbers, such as "72 GB of 100 GB"

variants.caption: Inline label — label, bar and value on one row
Segmented — discrete steps, as in password strength

usageNotes: Use a Meter for a measurement in a fixed range and a Progress bar for how much of a task is done. <meter> and <progress> are different elements with different meanings.
Set min, max and value, and use low, high and optimum to mark good and bad ranges. A custom meter needs role="meter" with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuenow, as in the APG Meter pattern.
Give it an accessible name with a <label>. If the number alone isn't meaningful, add aria-valuetext, such as "72 GB of 100 GB".
Show the value as text too, and don't use color alone to say a value is good or bad (WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color). Keep the fill at 3:1 contrast against the track (WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast).
A Meter only displays a value. If people should set it, use a Slider.
frameworkNotes: Only Apple ships a separate meter-type component.
htmlOutline:
<label for="disk">Disk usage</label>
<meter id="disk" min="0" max="100" low="60" high="85" value="72">72%</meter>
